item.title: The shift toward open and reproducible AI research
item.description: Abstract The reproducibility crisis has directed the AI research community toward improving documentation practices. Several studies have identified methodological issues, and in response, the most impactful venues in the field have introduced reproducibility checklists. item.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
item.description: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. item.title: MLOps-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Production ML Engineering in Real Repositories
item.description: AI agents are increasingly expected to modify and maintain machine-learning systems in production, yet existing benchmarks primarily evaluate either competition-style ML experimentation or generic repository issue resolution. item.title: Development of an LLM-Based System for Automatic Code Generation from HEP Publications
item.description: Ensuring the reproducibility of physics results is one of the crucial challenges in high-energy physics (HEP). item.description: Prompt engineering is increasingly used across Software Engineering (SE) activities, including requirements analysis, coding, testing, documentation, repository analysis, and planning. item.description: Coding agents use execution harnesses to constrain the consequences of prompt injection by enforcing permission boundaries. item.description: GB-scale large apps like on-device LLMs and rich media editors are becoming the next-generation trend, but their heavy memory and I/O demands, especially during multitasking, cause devices to reclaim or kill processes, turning warm apps into cold launches.
